newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes weaken for sour differentials.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes weaken for sour differentials.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes were weaker for sweet grades in Friday afternoon activity, while sour barrels attracted bids at steady levels, traders said.

Cash markets were quiet after a relatively active morning session when Light Louisiana Sweet was sold at 20-25 cents over the April West Texas Intermediate/Cushing. Since that time the LLS has moved lower, talked at 15-20 cts over WTI.

Traders said the softer values for LLS may be related to talk of refinery troubles at a plant in the U.S. Gulf. Verification of the market talk could not be immediately confirmed, but LLS prices have remained 5-10 cts lower.
April WTI/Cushing lost around 10 cts from midday, ranging around the $20.55-65 a barrel level. NYMEX losses stemmed from technical selling and weakness in the prompt heating oil.
For the grades, Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was flat to 20 cts under the WTI/Cushing, while Midland/WTI was valued at 35 cts below the same marker.
West Texas Sour/Midland sold at WTI/Cushing -$2.45, steady with the weaker values seen from Thursday.
Eugene Island barrels also sold at WTI/Cushing -$2.35, traders said.
The Apr/May spread remained steady from the morning at 20 cts, keeping Apr Postings Plus at Cushing +$1.95-98.
